events.title: First Performance of 'Silent Night'
events.description: The Christmas carol 'Stille Nacht' was first performed at the Church of St. Nicholas in Oberndorf, Austria, with lyrics by Joseph Mohr and music by Franz Xaver Gruber.
events.significance: It became one of the most widely recognized and translated Christmas carols in the world, and was added to UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2011.

events.title: Treaty of Ghent Signed
events.description: Representatives of the United States and Great Britain signed the Treaty of Ghent in Belgium, ending the War of 1812.
events.significance: The treaty restored prewar boundaries and ushered in a lasting era of peaceful relations between the United States and Britain, though news of it arrived too late to prevent the Battle of New Orleans.

events.title: Library of Congress Fire
events.description: A fire in the Capitol building destroyed about two-thirds of the Library of Congress collection, including much of Thomas Jefferson's original library.
events.significance: The loss led to a major rebuilding and expansion effort, helping shape the Library of Congress into the world's largest library.

events.title: Apollo 8 Orbits the Moon and Broadcasts Christmas Eve Message
events.description: Apollo 8 astronauts Frank Borman, Jim Lovell, and William Anders became the first humans to orbit the Moon and read from the Book of Genesis in a live broadcast on Christmas Eve, and the crew photographed Earthrise.
events.significance: The mission was a key step toward the Apollo 11 lunar landing, and the Earthrise photograph became one of the most influential images in history, shaping global environmental awareness.

events.title: First Ariane Rocket Launched
events.description: The European Space Agency launched the first Ariane 1 rocket from Kourou, French Guiana, on its maiden flight.
events.significance: The Ariane program established Europe as a major player in commercial space launch and gave it independent access to space.
